name: CEIL (Compositional Exemplars for In-context Learning)
venue: ICML 2023 (Proceedings of the 40th International Conference on Machine Learning, PMLR v202)
authors_affiliation: Jiacheng Ye, Zhiyong Wu, Jiangtao Feng, Tao Yu, Lingpeng Kong. Affiliations (per PMLR v202): (1) Department of Computer Science, The University of Hong Kong (Jiacheng Ye, Tao Yu, Lingpeng Kong); (2) Shark-NLP, Shanghai Artificial Intelligence Laboratory (Zhiyong Wu, Jiangtao Feng).
task_domain: In-context demonstration retrieval / exemplar selection for NLP in-context learning (ICL), spanning text classification (sentiment analysis, paraphrase detection, NLI, commonsense reasoning) and generation (open-domain QA, code generation, semantic parsing). Not an agent/planning task.
problem_setting: Offline, non-interactive, single-pass in-context example selection. A frozen black-box LM performs ICL; the goal is to select a subset of K demonstrations from a training set (index) to maximize the LM's likelihood of the correct answer for a given test input. Supervision is the LM's own score over candidate subsets (no human labels for the optimal subset). The retriever (a learnable conditional-DPP / metric-learning encoder) is trained offline per task; at inference the LM weights are never updated.
what_is_retrieved: demos (in-context examples, i.e., input-output exemplar pairs from the training set), selected jointly as a SUBSET rather than independently.
retrieval_grounding: STATIC external corpus: the retrievable store is the task's fixed training set (deduplicated). No growing/episodic agent memory is written; the store is frozen.
completeness_vs_topk_objective: Subset-completeness oriented rather than independent top-k: in-context example selection is recast as a SUBSET selection problem, modeling the joint probability of the whole exemplar set with a conditional DPP and selecting via MAP inference to jointly optimize relevance and inter-example diversity (compositional coverage). K is still a fixed budget per task, but the selection objective is set-level (det of the kernel sub-matrix) not per-item top-k.
cbr_cycle_coverage: N/A (not framed as CBR; only a Retrieve-then-Reuse pattern would apply: Retrieve = yes, Reuse = verbatim ICL exemplars, Revise = no, Retain = no).
explicit_cbr_grounding: False. CEIL does not frame itself as case-based reasoning and does not cite Aamodt & Plaza / Kolodner; it frames demo selection as DPP subset selection / metric learning.
retrieval_unit: single demonstration (input-output example) as the atomic item, but the retrieved/selected unit is a SUBSET (set) of such demonstrations jointly modeled by a conditional DPP.
index_source: Static corpus: the task training set, deduplicated (truncated to ~44,000 instances following Rubin et al. 2022 to reduce scoring cost). Offline-induced; not online/test-time-induced.
index_structure_topology: Flat vector index over training-set examples encoded by a learnable BERT-based dual encoder (dot-product kernel). A two-stage scheme is used: a KNN/dense retriever first narrows N candidates to n (e.g., n=100), then the DPP kernel (PSD matrix L over those candidates) defines set probabilities; no graph or hierarchy.
retriever_type: Learned dense retriever instantiated as a conditional Determinantal Point Process (DPP) with learnable BERT-based embedders (metric learning); dot-product (linear) kernel as relevance/similarity function. Initialized from EPR. Baselines include BM25 (sparse), TopK-BERT/Contriever/SimCSE (off-the-shelf dense), DPP-BERT (DPP on frozen BERT), and EPR (learned).
retriever_learning_signal: Downstream-task-effectiveness / LM-preference via contrastive learning. Each sampled candidate subset is scored by the frozen inference LM as s_ij = P_LM(y_i | S_ij, x_i) (probability of the correct answer given the subset). A fine-grained pair-wise margin (ranking) loss trains the DPP so that 'better' subsets get higher det-probability than 'worse' ones; margin is scaled by the LM-score rank difference. (InfoNCE is also studied as an alternative loss.) No RL.
query_construction: Raw test input is encoded by the input embedder; the conditioned (relevance-modulated) DPP kernel is L_tilde = Diag(r) L Diag(r) where r_i = g(a_i, x) is the relevance of candidate i to the test input x. Candidate examples are encoded by concatenating all instance texts except labels.
query_granularity: task-level (one-shot at t=0): a single retrieval/selection of the exemplar subset per test input before generation; no iterative or step-level querying.
when_to_retrieve: one-shot: select the exemplar subset once per test instance, then the frozen LM generates the answer in a single pass.
retrieval_trigger_signal: Fixed schedule (always retrieve once per test input before inference); no confidence/uncertainty-triggered or learned-router triggering.
reranking: MAP inference acts as a joint selection/ranking step: after a KNN retriever narrows N to n candidates, an exact greedy DPP-MAP algorithm (O(nK) per iteration via incremental Cholesky updates) greedily selects K examples by maximal incremental log-det gain, jointly balancing relevance and diversity. This effectively replaces top-k with a set-level DPP rerank/selection (DPP-MAP vs TOPK is ablated, Table 6).
retrieved_context_refinement: Selected exemplars are sorted by similarity to the input in ascending order before being concatenated into the prompt (common practice); otherwise no decomposition/compression/distillation. The DPP diversity term itself reduces redundancy/distractors within the selected set.
index_content_separation: N/A (full example texts are both indexed and loaded; two-stage KNN->DPP narrows candidates for efficiency but not an index/content separation).
how_retrieved_used: Prompt augmentation: the selected exemplar subset is concatenated as the in-context demonstration prompt for a frozen black-box LM (GPT-Neo 2.7B primarily; also GPT2-XL 1.5B and Codex 175B). For classification, tasks are reframed as multiple choice (compare LM likelihood of each labeled option); for generation, greedy decoding. The LM-score over subsets is also used as the training signal for the retriever.
planning_integration: N/A for planning/acting; integration is one-shot exemplars at prediction time (retrieve-then-predict). Not embedded in any search/MCTS or multi-step plan.
reasoning_search_interleaving_granularit: per-answer: a single retrieval feeds one LM forward pass per test instance; no per-step or per-token interleaving.
adaptation_mechanism: verbatim ICL exemplar (retrieved examples are used as-is in the prompt; no case adaptation/revision).
retrieved_item_representation: raw demonstrations (input-output example pairs) injected verbatim as prompt text; for classification, candidate label names are appended as options.
abstraction_level_of_retrieved_unit: raw single demonstrations (concrete input-output examples), but selected as a composed set; not distilled strategies, rules, workflows, or programs.
noise_robustness_mechanism: Retriever-aware training (contrastive learning aligns embeddings/DPP-score with actual LM usefulness) plus the DPP diversity term that suppresses redundant/overlapping exemplars; selecting a compact, mutually-diverse subset reduces uninformative/duplicate context. No explicit self-reflection or distractor-filtering module.
memory_type: none (static training-set index; no episodic/skill/workflow memory).
write_back: False. The system does not store new experiences/cases/skills; the retriever is trained offline and the index is the frozen training set.
online_growth: False. The retrievable store does not grow during deployment/test-time; it is frozen after offline induction.
failure_experience_usage: No explicit storage of failed experiences. Training uses a contrastive pair-wise margin over candidate subsets ranked by LM score, so relatively 'worse' (lower-LM-score) subsets serve as negatives within the contrastive loss, but failures are not retained in any memory.
memory_evolution_update: N/A (no memory; store is append-free/static after offline construction).
retrieval_as_learned_policy: Partially: subset selection is a LEARNED conditional-DPP scorer trained by contrastive LM-preference (metric learning), and selection uses DPP-MAP greedy inference rather than fixed similarity top-k. It is not an RL/value-based policy (no M-MDP or Q-learning); the learned object is a DPP probability model over subsets.
cross_agent_or_cross_framework_sharing: No multi-agent sharing. However the paper demonstrates transferability: a retriever trained for one LM (e.g., GPT-Neo) transfers to other LMs (GPT2-XL, Codex), and a retriever trained on one dataset partially transfers to related datasets (e.g., across NLI tasks, and among code/semantic-parsing tasks).
benchmarks: 12 datasets across 7 NLP tasks: SST-5, MRPC, QNLI, MNLI, CMSQA (CommonsenseQA), HellaSwag, WebQs, GeoQuery, NL2Bash, Break, MTOP, SMCalFlow. Compositional splits: GeoQuery (Standard/Template/TMCD/Length) and SMCalFlow-CS (0-S, 0-C, 8-C, 16-C, 32-C).
benchmark_family: QA / NLU+generation: sentiment (SST-5), paraphrase (MRPC), NLI (QNLI, MNLI), commonsense reasoning (CMSQA, HellaSwag), open-domain QA (WebQs), code generation (GeoQuery, NL2Bash), semantic parsing (Break, MTOP, SMCalFlow). Not agent/web/embodied/tool benchmarks. Includes compositional-generalization splits.
baselines: Learning-free: RANDOM, TOPK-BM25, TOPK-BERT, DPP-BERT, TOPK-CONTRIEVER, TOPK-SIMCSE. Learning-based: EPR (Rubin et al. 2022, singleton example scorer). Compositional comparisons (Table 3): T5-Base+CSL-Aug (Qiu et al. 2022a), Cover-LS (Levy et al. 2022), PaLM 540B and PaLM 540B (Oracle) (Qiu et al. 2022b).
key_metrics: Accuracy for classification tasks; Exact Match (EM) for WebQs/GeoQuery/NL2Bash/MTOP/SMCalFlow; LF-EM for Break. Also MRR of top-K candidates (training-data construction ablation) and retrieval latency (seconds).
headline_result: Using GPT-Neo 2.7B as inferencer, CEIL achieves an average of 56.76 across the 12 datasets vs 53.37 for EPR (the strongest learned baseline), a +3.39 absolute average gain (state-of-the-art over all baselines); especially strong on NLI (>20% absolute over learning-free baselines, e.g., QNLI 85.41 and MNLI 71.74).
ablations: (1) Inference algorithm (Table 6): DPP-MAP vs TOPK on BERT/EPR/CEIL; DPP-MAP helps more for learned retrievers (DPP-CEIL avg gains over TOPK-CEIL), showing the value of aligning embedding similarity to LM usefulness. (2) Initialization & loss (Table 5): EPR-init >> BERT-init; pair-wise margin loss beats InfoNCE notably on generation tasks (~+4% GeoQuery, ~+6% MTOP). (3) Training-data construction (Table 4): TOP100+RAND sampling with C=50 candidates best; k-DPP sampling worse. (4) Number of in-context examples (Fig 3 Left): classification benefits from fewer/compact sets; CEIL matches EPR/TOPK-BERT-with-32-examples using merely ~4 / ~1 example. (5) Trade-off factor lambda (Fig 3 Right): diversity matters more for harder tasks (NLI, semantic parsing), relevance more for simpler tasks (sentiment). (6) Transferability across LMs and datasets (Fig 2).
evaluation_decoupling: Mostly end-to-end task metrics. Intrinsic retrieval quality is reported in a limited way (MRR of top-K candidates in the training-data construction ablation, Table 4) but not as a primary decoupled Recall@k/nDCG evaluation; main results are downstream task accuracy/EM.
process_vs_outcome_metrics: Primarily outcome metrics (final task accuracy/EM/LF-EM). Some process-oriented signals: MRR of candidate ranking and compositional-split performance, but no reasoning-faithfulness or step-wise process scoring.
cost_efficiency_tradeoff: DPP-MAP adds negligible latency over KNN top-k because n and K are small (e.g., n=100, K=16); measured retrieval latency for 50 in-context examples on SST5 is 30s (TOPK) vs 36s (DPP-MAP), ~1.2x. The pair-wise ranking loss avoids computing the O(N^3) DPP normalization det(L+I). Training: 30 epochs, batch 128, lr 1e-5 on 2x NVIDIA A100 GPUs; greedy DPP-MAP is O(nK) per iteration via incremental Cholesky. Compactness benefit: CEIL matches 32-example baselines using ~1-4 examples, cutting quadratic attention cost.
context_budget_and_selection_count: Fixed-k budget capped by LM context length: nominal 50 in-context examples, truncated to the LM max context (1,024 for GPT2-XL, 2,048 for GPT-Neo, 8,001 for Codex), giving average #ICE per task ~22-50 (e.g., SST-5 40, MRPC 27, SMCalFlow 22). Candidate narrowing n (e.g., 100) then DPP-MAP greedily selects K (e.g., 16 during training subsets).
benchmark_construction_and_size: N/A (uses existing datasets, not a newly constructed benchmark; dataset sizes are reported in Table 1, e.g., MNLI 392,568 train, SMCalFlow 102,491 train).
builds_on: EPR (Rubin et al. 2022, Efficient Prompt Retrieval / learning-to-retrieve singleton in-context examples via contrastive LM-feedback) which CEIL extends from single-example to set-level selection and uses as encoder initialization; Determinantal Point Processes (Kulesza & Taskar; Chen et al. 2018 greedy MAP); KATE / kNN dense demo retrieval (Liu et al. 2022).
contrasts_with: EPR and other independent top-k demo retrievers (TOPK-BERT/BM25/Contriever/SimCSE) that select examples independently without modeling inter-example interaction; Cover-LS (Levy et al. 2022) which uses a specially-trained subphrase predictor + task-specific DPP diversity not aligned with the LM; compositional data-augmentation methods (Qiu et al. 2022a CSL-Aug); multi-pass ICL aggregation methods (Shi et al. 2022; Li et al. 2022) which need multiple test-time inferences.
lineage: Group A (ICL demonstration retrieval): a learning-based, set-level demonstration retriever that advances the lineage from heuristic/similarity top-k selection (KATE) -> learned singleton retrieval (EPR) -> learned compositional subset retrieval (CEIL via conditional DPP + contrastive LM preference), establishing joint relevance+diversity demo selection.
